title: Tower Maze Defense (v32)
description: A tower-defense maze game where you build towers along a winding path to stop waves of enemies. Features branching paths, boss enemies, buff towers, and a seed-based map generator.
prompt:
Redesign the game UI layout so the gameplay canvas is the main focus and the tower/unit selection is moved into a horizontal panel underneath the game board.

Current problem:
The right sidebar is too cluttered. It contains the unit selection, stats, seed, buttons and info, which makes the page crowded and causes scrolling. I want the unit selection removed from the right sidebar entirely and placed below the gameplay area.

Layout requirements:
1. Put the game canvas on the left/top as the main area.
2. Move ALL tower/unit selection buttons to a new bottom toolbar directly underneath the game canvas.
3. The bottom unit toolbar should span the same width as the game canvas.
4. Arrange unit buttons horizontally in compact groups:
   - Attack: Arrow, Cannon, Ice, Laser, Tesla
   - Buff: Range+, Speed+, Power+
   - Economy: Mint
5. Use small compact cards for unit buttons, with icon, short name and cost only.
6. The bottom toolbar should not make the page wider than the canvas and should wrap neatly if the screen is small.
7. Keep the right sidebar, but make it much narrower and simpler.
8. The right sidebar should only contain:
   - Difficulty badge
   - Compact stats row
   - Seed
   - Selected tower/enemy info
   - Upgrade/delete/target options when needed
9. Remove tower/unit selection from the right sidebar completely.

Action button changes:
1. Move the wave, new map, pause and speed controls into a small compact control row near the top of the right sidebar or just above the bottom toolbar.
2. Make the buttons icon-only:
   - Wave button: ▶
   - New Map button: 🗺
   - Pause/Play button: ⏸ or ▶
   - Speed button: 1x / 2x / 5x
3. These buttons should be small square or pill buttons, not large full-width buttons.
4. Do not use text labels like “Wave”, “New Map” or “Pause” on the buttons.
5. Add tooltip/title text so users can still understand the icons on hover.

Visual design:
1. The UI should fit on one screen without vertical scrolling on a normal desktop viewport.
2. Keep the dark sci-fi style.
3. Reduce padding, gaps and font sizes in the side panel.
4. Make the bottom tower toolbar visually distinct, like a dock or command bar.
5. Use section labels but keep them compact.
6. Selected tower buttons should still show a highlight.
7. Disabled/unaffordable tower buttons should still look dimmed.

Responsive behaviour:
1. On desktop, use this structure:
   - Main content area: game canvas
   - Bottom dock under canvas: tower/unit selection
   - Right compact sidebar: stats, seed, info and controls
2. On smaller screens, stack the sidebar under the canvas and keep the unit toolbar under the canvas.
3. Avoid any layout that pushes all tower buttons back into the right sidebar.
